🩸 Blood and Flesh Combining — Rabbi Yehoshua's principle, and Rav Zeira's 'same animal' condition
🏛️ Three Roman Decrees — Rabbi Reuven ben Isterobeli's clever strategy to get them nullified

overview.title: 📖 Overview: From Measures to Miracles
overview.subtitle: Meilah 17a–17b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Rava closes yesterday's question by clarifying that the Torah's juxtaposition of kosher/non-kosher animals with creeping things applies only to the prohibition of 'you shall not make yourselves detestable,' not to their measures — so there is no basis to split kosher and non-kosher carcasses into different impurity-measures. A new mishna then states Rabbi Yehoshua's principle: only items sharing both the same TYPE of impurity and the same MEASURE combine. This leads into a striking historical narrative — Rabbi Matya ben Ḥarash's question about the source for blood-of-creeping-animals impurity, traced back to Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yosei, and the story of how Roman decrees against Shabbat, circumcision, and family purity were nullified, first cleverly by Rabbi Reuven ben Isterobeli, and then — after the decrees were reinstated — through Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai's journey to Rome, aided by a demon named ben Temalyon.

slides.title: ⚖️ Rava's Answer: One Prohibition, Not Different Measures
slides.subtitle: Resolving Rav Adda bar Ahava's challenge from the end of yesterday's daf
slides.hebrewSource: כִּי קָא מַקֵּישׁ רַחֲמָנָא – לְבַל תְּשַׁקְּצוּ, אֲבָל לְשִׁיעוּרִין – לָא
slides.label: The resolution:
slides.text: When the Torah (Leviticus 20:25) juxtaposes kosher and non-kosher animals with creeping things, that comparison teaches only that all three share the single prohibition 'you shall not make yourselves detestable.' It does NOT mean their MEASURES for impurity must also be compared or split apart. So unlike the eight special creeping animals (which the Torah does textually distinguish for measure purposes), kosher and non-kosher animal carcasses share the identical olive-bulk measure for impurity — there is no room to invent a separate, larger measure for non-kosher carcasses.

slides.title: 🩸 When Do Different Sources of Impurity Combine?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yehoshua's principle, tested and refined
rows: Two halves of an olive-bulk from two different corpses/carcasses
Creeping animal + animal carcass (both impure until evening)
Blood + flesh from the SAME creeping animal
Yes — 'the significance of an entire animal' (Rav Yosef)
Blood + flesh, each only PART of a (possibly different) animal
No, per Rav Zeira — though a baraita seems to disagree until reconciled

callout.label: Rav Yosef's reconciliation:
callout.text: A challenging baraita ('the impure ones' teaches they combine, even from two different creeping animals) is limited to combinations drawn from WHOLE animals; Rav Zeira's stricter rule governs when only partial amounts from each are involved.

slides.title: 🏛️ Rabbi Reuven ben Isterobeli's Clever Strategy
slides.subtitle: Nullifying three Roman decrees with a single line of reasoning, three times

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rome decreed: no Shabbat observance, no circumcision, no family purity laws. Rabbi Reuven ben Isterobeli disguised himself and sat among the Roman officials
2️⃣ On Shabbat: 'Doesn't an enemy's poverty please you? Then let the Jews rest and not work — they'll grow poor!' They agreed and canceled the decree
3️⃣ On circumcision: 'Doesn't an enemy's weakness please you? Then let them circumcise their sons and weaken them!' Canceled again
4️⃣ On family purity: 'Doesn't an enemy's decline please you? Then let them refrain from their wives when impure, so they won't multiply!' Canceled a third time
5️⃣ Twist: the Romans then recognized he was a Jew and reinstated all three decrees — setting up the need for a new mission to Rome

slides.title: ✡️ Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai's Mission to Rome
slides.subtitle: A dangerous journey, a demon's help, and torn decrees

nodes.content: 🕊️ Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai, 'accustomed to miracles,' volunteers to go to Rome with Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yosei, despite the danger
😔 En route, Rabbi Elazar whispers the answer to a Torah question in his teacher's presence — a breach of etiquette. Rabbi Shimon, upset, says he won't return home
👻 A demon, ben Temalyon, offers to help by possessing the emperor's daughter in advance. Rabbi Shimon tearfully accepts, noting even a demon's help is a form of divine kindness
🗣️ Arriving in Rome, Rabbi Shimon commands: 'Ben Temalyon, emerge!' — the demon leaves the emperor's daughter, healing her instantly
🎁 The grateful emperor offers any reward and opens his treasury. In it, they find the decree — and tear it up, nullifying it for good

slides.title: 🚫 New Mishna: Piggul and Notar — Two Names, Two Rules
slides.subtitle: They don't combine for impurity, but DO combine for the eating prohibition
rows: No — considered 'two separate names/categories,' and this rule is only rabbinic
Rabbi Eliezer: 'It shall not be eaten because it is sacred' (Ex. 29:34) applies broadly to anything sacred that was disqualified
Creeping animal + animal carcass, or animal carcass + human corpse, for impurity
No — not even for the more lenient measure
New mishna, continuing Rabbi Yehoshua's principle

summary.principle: Whether different sources of impurity or prohibition combine to reach a liability threshold depends on precise textual and conceptual alignment — same impurity, same measure, or a shared underlying prohibition — a rigor mirrored in the era's history, where Rabbi Reuven ben Isterobeli's clever rhetoric and Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai's perilous mission to Rome each achieved, through very different means, the nullification of a harsh decree.

🎓 Key Principle: precision in law and courage in history both served the same goal — protecting the community from what threatened it

quiz.q: According to Rava, what does the Torah's juxtaposition of kosher/non-kosher animals with creeping animals (Leviticus 20:25) actually teach?
o: That they all share the same measure for impurity
That they all share the single prohibition of 'you shall not make yourselves detestable,' but NOT that their measures must differ
That non-kosher animals require a larger measure than kosher ones
Nothing — the verse is purely descriptive
quiz.e: Rava clarifies that the juxtaposition establishes a shared prohibition, not a basis for distinguishing measures — so kosher and non-kosher carcasses retain the same olive-bulk measure.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yehoshua's principle in the new mishna, what two conditions must be met for two sources of impurity to combine toward the requisite measure?
o: They must come from the same species and the same city
They must share both the same TYPE/duration of impurity and the same MEASURE
They must both be from creeping animals
There are no conditions; everything always combines
quiz.e: Rabbi Yehoshua teaches that only items equal in both the nature of the impurity they impart and the measure required to impart it will combine to reach the requisite threshold.

quiz.q: What clever argument did Rabbi Reuven ben Isterobeli use to convince the Romans to cancel their decree against Shabbat observance?
o: He argued that Shabbat observance was economically beneficial to Rome
He argued that if the Romans wanted their enemies (the Jews) to become poor, they should let them rest on Shabbat and not work, which would impoverish them
He bribed the Roman officials
He threatened rebellion
quiz.e: Rabbi Reuven ben Isterobeli used reverse psychology, framing Shabbat observance, circumcision, and family purity practices as things that would actually weaken or impoverish the Jewish people, appealing to Roman self-interest.

quiz.q: How did Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai ultimately cure the Roman emperor's daughter and gain access to nullify the decree?
o: Through a potion he brewed
By commanding the demon ben Temalyon, who had possessed her in advance to help the mission, to emerge from her
By bribing Roman physicians
The daughter was never actually ill
quiz.e: The demon ben Temalyon had possessed the emperor's daughter beforehand to assist the mission; Rabbi Shimon's command caused the demon to leave, healing her and earning the emperor's gratitude.

quiz.q: According to Shmuel, in what context do piggul and notar NOT combine, and according to Rabbi Eliezer, in what context DO they combine?
o: They never combine for any purpose
They don't combine for ritual impurity of the hands (a rabbinic law); they DO combine for the Torah prohibition on eating disqualified sacred food
They always combine for every purpose
They combine only when eaten together in the same meal
quiz.e: Shmuel limits the mishna's 'do not combine' ruling to hand-impurity (rabbinic), while Rabbi Eliezer's derivation from Exodus 29:34 shows that for the eating prohibition itself, piggul and notar do combine to reach the liability measure.
